title: Trunk segment masses (thorax/abdomen/pelvis) of living males by MRI

quantity.name: segment mass
quantity.definition: mass of thorax, abdomen, pelvis and whole trunk as % body mass and in grams

source.authors: Pearsall DJ, Reid JG, Ross R
source.sample: 26 males; 26 living adult males, MRI (Philips 1.5 T), prone, arms above head; 10-mm slices every 50 mm
source.notes: height SD 5.7 cm; body mass SD 16.8 kg (range 56.4-129 kg); BMI 28.6 ± 4.8 (range 19.7-39.3). DOI not printed in PDF (likely 10.1007/BF02368294 – verify).

protocol.summary: In vivo MRI segment parameters of the trunk of 26 males; tissue-specific densities; mean, SD, min, max.
how_to_use: Assign thorax/abdomen/pelvis masses as 13.0/16.0/13.3 % body mass (trunk 42.2 %) for an average male; segment boundaries as in notes.
For heavier/lighter subjects prefer the Fig 3 linear regressions on body mass (slopes 0.11/0.22/0.14 for thorax/abdomen/pelvis): the abdomen absorbs most extra mass.
Use min-max range (trunk 35.8-48.0 % BM) for robustness/sensitivity runs.
Note in vivo thorax density 0.82 g/cc (lungs) – much lower than cadaver-based 1.01 g/cc used by volumetric methods.

measurement.device: Philips Gyroscan 1.5 T; tissue densities assigned per pixel (cortical bone 1.8, cancellous 1.1, viscera/muscle/blood 1.06, adipose 0.96, lung 0.25 g/cc)

equations: Table 2 (printed, M in g; HT cm; Mass kg): Trunk M = 26371.4 - 182*HT + 525.8*Mass (r2 0.87, SE 3404.3)
Table 2: Thorax M = 12922.8 - 68.3*HT + 1119.4*Mass (r2 0.64, SE 1465.6)  [as printed; does NOT reproduce the sample mean thorax mass – mass coefficient 1119.4 is probably a misprint for 119.4]
Table 2: Pelvis M = 9293.1 - 56.7*HT + 179.2*Mass (r2 0.86, SE 1241.4)  [as printed; at sample means gives ~15000 g vs mean 11587 g – use with caution]
Fig 3 (segment mass and body mass both in g): Trunk = -3846.51 + 0.47*BM (r2 0.88); Thorax = 1625.33 + 0.11*BM (r2 0.63); Abdomen = -5249.27 + 0.22*BM (r2 0.76); Pelvis = -222.58 + 0.14*BM (r2 0.81)
Table 3 gives stepwise regressions on trunk circumferences/depths/widths (not transcribed; see paper)
protocol.notes: Thorax = suprasternal notch (~T4/5) to xiphoid (~T9); abdomen = xiphoid to umbilicus (~L3/4); pelvis = umbilicus to pubic symphysis/greater trochanter (incl. perineum, excl. thighs); trunk = sum. Boundaries follow Zatsiorsky & Seluyanov gamma-scan definitions (thus close to de Leva UPT/MPT/LPT).

extraction.check_notes: Re-read Table 1 and Table 2 from rendered page images (p.697, p.699) and Fig 3 equations from p.698 image; all values match. Table 2 thorax and pelvis mass equations do not reproduce sample means (printed as such).

pass_rule.rule: input data – not graded; use for robustness checks
